finding: NEW FINDING (not in the 2026-07-12 audit's 75-row matrix). portfolio_return_series silently treats a symbol's no-trade/gap day as a 0% return rather than excluding that day from the volatility/covariance calculation. For the current committed 10-symbol sample portfolio, 3 of 10 symbols (ABB, MSB, NAB) have 198-249 NaN days out of 1626 (12-15% of the sample) -- likely trading halts or thin-liquidity gaps for these smaller-cap names. This convention is internally consistent (confirmed this round: the ex-ante w^T Sigma w formula reproduces annual_volatility exactly once the SAME fillna(0.0)+ddof=0 convention is applied) and is not a bug, but it is undocumented and could understate realized volatility for symbols with a meaningful no-trade-day fraction, since a 0%-return day contributes nothing to variance versus what excluding it (increasing effective sample concentration around trading days) would do.
impact: Volatility/Sharpe for portfolios containing thinly-traded names may be understated by an unquantified amount; not previously flagged.
recommended_action: Document the convention explicitly in portfolio_return_series's docstring; consider reporting the NaN-day fraction per symbol alongside the risk report as a data-quality caveat.
acceptance_criteria: Convention documented; NaN-day fraction surfaced in output for any symbol above a materiality threshold (e.g. >5%).

sub_category: Daily automation blocked by macOS TCC (NEW)
finding: NEW FINDING (the daily_run.sh/LaunchAgent automation itself did not exist at the time of the original 2026-07-12 audit, so this is necessarily new). The LaunchAgent that should trigger scripts/daily_run.sh on schedule is installed and loads correctly, but macOS's TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) privacy protection for ~/Desktop blocks the launchd-spawned /bin/bash process from actually executing inside the project directory ('Operation not permitted'), confirmed via a documented controlled experiment (a job pointed at /tmp runs fine; the identical job pointed at ~/Desktop/... fails). This requires a one-time manual user action (System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk Access -> add /bin/bash) that cannot be performed by any script. Manual invocation (bash scripts/daily_run.sh) is unaffected and works normally.
impact: Until the user grants Full Disk Access, the 'automated' daily cycle silently does not run on schedule -- must be triggered by hand, which is easy to forget and would cause the alpha_score v2 shadow-log's '6 months continuous' review clock (PROJECT_STATE.md mục 3) to silently stall.
recommended_action: User must grant Full Disk Access to /bin/bash (2-minute one-time action, documented in PROJECT_STATE.md mục 4). No code fix possible.
acceptance_criteria: launchctl-triggered run appears in logs/daily_run.log without manual invocation.
verification_status: NEW -- documented in PROJECT_STATE.md (read this round); not independently re-tested (would require waiting for a real scheduled trigger, outside this round's scope).
